Sure, here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider what it means to one-hot encode a sequence. Each unique sequence of letters (in this case, DNA letters) will correspond to a unique dimension in the encoding. For a DNA string of 3,000 letters, think about how many possible sequences there are.

**Hint 2:** Remember that each position in the DNA string can be one of four letters: T, G, C, or A. When one-hot encoding the entire sequence, you need to account for every possible combination of these letters across all positions in the string.
